 7                SENATOR CARLUCCI:   Thank you, 

 8   Mr. President.

 9                The issue of toll evasion has become 

10   a real financial drain on commuters and taxpayers 

11   throughout New York State.  In fact, this really 

12   is not a victimless crime.  

13                What we've seen is that now about 

14   $16.5 million a year is being lost to chronic 

15   toll evasion.  And that's where someone goes 

16   through a toll where they know they're not going 

17   to pay that toll fee.  

18                And what we've done is allow for, in 

19   this legislation, to codify into the state laws 

20   that the DMV would be able to work with 

21   toll-collecting authorities to suspend someone's 

22   vehicle registration if they are a chronic toll 

23   evader.

24                The other very important piece of 

25   this legislation is it allows New York State to 


                                                                2096

 1   enter into interstate agreements to go after 

 2   chronic toll evaders that may reside outside of 

 3   New York State.  

 4                By passing this legislation, we will 

 5   be saving New York taxpayers millions of dollars 

 6   a year to taxpayers and commuters.  Let's pass 

 7   this legislation, get it passed in the Assembly, 

 8   on the Governor's desk and signed into law.  

 9                Thank you, Mr. President.

14                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

15   Kennedy to explain his vote.

16                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Thank you, 

17   Mr. President.  

18                This legislation at hand has one 

19   overarching goal:  to strengthen the penalties 

20   against those who are found guilty of possessing 

21   or promoting child pornography.  

22                Anyone who calls child pornography a 

23   victimless crime is either misguided or 

24   misinformed.  Child pornography inflicts 

25   long-lasting psychological damage on its victims, 


                                                                2112

 1   not only from the trauma of its creation but also 

 2   as a result of the knowledge that the images are 

 3   forever circulating on the Internet.  

 4                The statistics are alarming.  

 5   According to the New York State Division of 

 6   Criminal Justice Services, some studies have 

 7   shown that up to 40 percent of criminals arrested 

 8   for possession of child pornography have also 

 9   personally victimized children, with 15 percent 

10   more having attempted to solicit investigators 

11   who have posed as children online.

12                Right now in New York State 

13   possession of child pornography is classified as 

14   a Class E felony, and the maximum sentence that 

15   comes along with that charge is only four years 

16   in prison.  Through this legislation we're 

17   creating a new Class D felony charge for the 

18   possession and/or promotion of child pornography 

19   if victims involved in the pornography are 

20   underneath the age of 13, if it portrays sadistic 

21   or masochistic conduct, if there are 600 or more 

22   pornographic images found, or if there's an 

23   attempt to generate money off of those images.  

24                We wouldn't be moving this 

25   legislation forward without the community 


                                                                2113

 1   standing up and demanding it.  We've had a 

 2   tremendous amount of support from public safety 

 3   advocates like Buffalo Police Chief of Detectives 

 4   Dennis Richards, Detective Joe Ahmed from the 

 5   Buffalo Police Department as well, Cheektowaga 

 6   Police Lieutenant Ken Rusin and Detective Mike 

 7   Hockwater.  They're on the front lines every 

 8   single day, helping to keep our communities safe 

 9   and helping to ensure that victims of child 

10   pornography have a better day ahead and that 

11   those perpetrators of heinous crime are brought 

12   to justice.

13                Together we're standing together to 

14   deliver a strong message that enough is enough, 

15   that we're going to never tolerate the 

16   sexualization of our children in our communities 

17   and we're going to do everything we can as a 

18   state to ensure that this heinous crime is dealt 

19   with swiftly and abruptly.

20                Thank you, Mr. President.  I vote 

21   aye.
